preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is an integer between 1 and 500,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= p_i <= i for i in range(2, n + 1))
preconditions.description: For each edge (p_i, i+1), p_i is a valid parent vertex index (1 ≤ p_i ≤ i).

preconditions.expression: all(c_i in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv' for c_i in [c_2, c_3, ..., c_n])
preconditions.description: Each edge letter c_i is a lowercase English letter between 'a' and 'v' inclusive.
The input consists of exactly n lines: the first line is n, followed by (n-1) lines of edge definitions.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [str(answer[v]) for v in range(1, n + 1)]
postconditions.description: The output is a space-separated list of n integers, where answer[v] is the length of the longest simple path in the subtree of vertex v that forms a Dokhtar-kosh string.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= answer[v] <= 2 * (n - 1) for v in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: Each answer[v] is a non-negative integer representing the length of a path (number of edges), bounded by the maximum possible path length in the tree (2*(n-1)).

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(c == answer[v] for c in counts.values()) or any(v == counts[c] for c in counts) for counts in [collections.Counter(path_edges) for path_edges in get_all_paths(v)]) for v in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For each vertex v, answer[v] is the maximum length of a simple path in its subtree where the multiset of edge letters can be rearranged into a palindrome. This means the counts of each letter in the path must satisfy: at most one letter has an odd count (for odd-length paths) or all letters have even counts (for even-length paths).
